# Reading a node's latest resolved attribute bag

Two read surfaces answer with a node's most recent resolved attributes — the
values it actually computed with, inputs included. Neither requires folding the
event log by hand.

## The template

The first node cascades to itself and dispatches three times, so there is a
history of bags to be wrong about.

```yaml
name: latest-bag-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: counter
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 3}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: summary
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: counter
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          seen_count:
            type: integer
            source: "{{nodes.counter.attribute.count}}"
          note:
            type: string
            default: latest
```

## Read it

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/nodes/$NODE_ID"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/nodes/$IID/counter"
```

Both carry `latest_attributes`.

## What the product does

The counter dispatches three times, emitting the deltas `{count: 1}`,
`{count: 2}`, `{count: 3}`.

Both surfaces answer with the same bag:

```json
{"count": 3, "max": 3}
```

It is the most recent dispatch's bag, not an earlier one's, and it includes
`max` — a resolved input no emitted delta ever carried.

No single event in the feed carries that bag. An operator working from
`GET /v1/events` alone would have to fold three deltas together and add the
resolved inputs.

The second node's latest bag comes back the same way with its own resolved
values:

```json
{"note": "latest", "seen_count": 3}
```

The two read surfaces agree, so an operator debugging from a dashboard and one
debugging from the node route reconstruct the same state.
